title: Derived pullback and open extension transport explicit etale-origin witnesses
statement:
Use the finite coefficient datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $u:U\to X$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:U\hookrightarrow V$ open immersions into separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves and the bounded-below derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ have the explicit etale-origin witness $(L,\alpha)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$.

The canonical sheaf comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] induces a natural derived isomorphism
$$\kappa_u:\nu_U^*u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*\nu_X^*.$$
For every open immersion $e:S\hookrightarrow T$ among $i,j$, the sheaf comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] induces a natural derived isomorphism
$$\delta_e:\nu_T^*e^{\mathrm{et}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}e^{\mathrm{proet}}_!\nu_S^*$$
on $D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$; both open extensions are applied degreewise [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. These maps are the maps induced by their termwise sheaf comparisons on localization at quasi-isomorphisms, independently of the representing complexes. Put $L_u=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}L$ and $M=Lu^*K$. Then the following displayed pairs are etale-origin witnesses on the indicated schemes:
$$
\begin{aligned}
M &: (L_u,\alpha_u),\qquad \alpha_u=(Lu^*\alpha)\circ\kappa_{u,L},\\
j_!K &: (j^{\mathrm{et}}_!L,\ j_!\alpha\circ\delta_{j,L}),\\
i_!M &: (i^{\mathrm{et}}_!L_u,\ i_!\alpha_u\circ\delta_{i,L_u}).
\end{aligned}
$$
All these objects and witnesses are bounded below.

proof.text: Use the published exact fixed-scalar inverse-image functors Etale.upperStar, ProEtale.upperStar and ProEtale.comparisonUpperStar. proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functors in steps 1 and 2. Their termwise functors carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors on the derived categories, with the stated natural identifications on representing complexes. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the induced functor for $u^*$ is precisely the $Lu^*$ in the statement. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] to every one of these exact functors: $\mathcal H^r(F_D B)\cong F(\mathcal H^rB)$. Hence, whenever $\mathcal H^r(B)=0$ for $r<N$, the same is true after any of these operations and their composites. They therefore restrict to the indicated $D^+$ categories. This uses cohomological boundedness, so an arbitrary representative of $B$ need not itself vanish in low degrees. In Lean these are Functor.mapDerivedCategory and Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlus; the latter stores the bounded-below condition.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); termwise localization and its cohomology comparison

proof.text: Let $C$ be a complex of etale $A$-module sheaves on $X$. Apply the natural sheaf isomorphism $c_u$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] in every degree. Each component $c_{u,C^r}$ is $A$-linear: both composites act on fixed-$A$ module sheaves by applying the functors to each scalar endomorphism $\lambda_a$ ($a\in A$) as in step 1, and naturality of $c_u$ for the sheaf maps $\lambda_a$ says exactly that $c_{u,C^r}$ commutes with them. Its naturality for $d_C^r$ says $u_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_X^*(d_C^r)\,c_{u,C^r}=c_{u,C^{r+1}}\,\nu_U^*u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}(d_C^r)$, so these components define a chain map. The inverse sheaf comparisons form its chain inverse. Naturality for each component of a chain map gives naturality on complexes. After localization these are isomorphisms between the two composites of step 3. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts this natural isomorphism uniquely through the localization of the source complexes, using the factorization isomorphisms of step 3. This is $\kappa_u$, with the pro-etale inverse image identified with $Lu^*$ as above. The lift evaluated on $QC$ is exactly the localized termwise comparison under those factorization isomorphisms. The uniqueness assertion and part (3) of the same lemma show that the construction is independent of the representing complex. Concretely apply Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to supportSiteComparisonCoefficientPullbackIso, conjugate by the inverse and forward mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, and whisker left by DerivedCategory.Plus.ι. This is definitionally the required normalization.

proof.text:
Put $L_u=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}L$ and $M=Lu^*K$. Step 4 gives $\kappa_{u,L}:
u_U^*L_u\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*
u_X^*L$. Applying the functor $Lu^*$ to the given isomorphism $\alpha$ gives an isomorphism $Lu^*\alpha:Lu^*
u_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, whose inverse is $Lu^*(\alpha^{-1})$. Their composite is $\alpha_u=(Lu^*\alpha)\circ\kappa_{u,L}$, with inverse $\kappa_{u,L}^{-1}\circ Lu^*(\alpha^{-1})$. This has source $
u_U^*L_u$ and target $M$, so $(L_u,\alpha_u)$ is the witness of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Both objects are bounded below by step 3. Construct pulled.complex and pulled.iso explicitly; pulled_complex is rfl and pulled_iso is HEq.rfl.

proof.text:
For any witness $(B, eta:
u_S^*B\xrightarrow{\sim}N)$ just considered, step 5 gives $\delta_{e,B}:
u_T^*e_!^{\mathrm{et}}B\xrightarrow{\sim}e_!^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_S^*B$. Composing with $e_!^{\mathrm{proet}} eta$ gives an isomorphism to $e_!^{\mathrm{proet}}N$; its inverse is $\delta_{e,B}^{-1}\circ e_!^{\mathrm{proet}}( eta^{-1})$. This is exactly the data required by [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Substituting $(e,B,N, eta)=(j,L,K,\alpha)$ gives the second displayed pair. Substituting $(e,B,N, eta)=(i,L_u,M,\alpha_u)$ gives the third. Choose an integer $N_0$ below the cohomology of both original objects $L,K$ (take the smaller of their two lower bounds). Step 3 shows that $L_u,M,j_!^{\mathrm{et}}L,j_!K,i_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_u,i_!M$ and all comparison sources belong to $D^{\ge N_0}$. Thus all three pairs are bounded below witnesses, with the exact formulas asserted. Construct the other two FixedEtaleOriginWitness records explicitly; all retained-complex and HEq equalities are reflexivity. Carry out the construction locally for an arbitrary commutative ring before specializing to ULift T.coefficientRing, avoiding expansion of the concrete coefficient ring.
